answer: Answer: The supplied zero-psi reading alone does not establish the pressure history at the load-bearing cylinder or prove when hydraulic support was lost. The zero reading comes from earlier synthetic test records, not a partner raw pressure trace. The more specific incident evidence is GTDE-03_hydraulic_isolation_followup.md, Reported findings: after B-system shutdown and isolation, the R3 isolation valve was reported to have slow bleed-through; the investigation concluded fluid could return through the feed and loss of hydraulic support could allow the yoke to drift downward under gravity. GTDE-02_extended_video_review.md reports approximately two hours of downward yoke movement while the carrier beam remained wedged against the spreader/posts. Source class: controlled benchmark derivatives of partner investigation findings; the gauge value is separately a synthetic scenario fact. Limit: No raw pressure historian, cylinder pressure time series, valve bench test, leak-down rate or displacement calculation was supplied. The records therefore support the reported drift mechanism but cannot quantify residual pressure at any instant. Residual pressure should remain unquantified, rather than being asserted absent solely from the gauge record.
